findings.note: She is listed as a sponsor of HB 788, Fix Our Democracy (primary sponsors: Buansi, Willingham, Cohn, Rubin). The date is the bill's filing date; the date she joined is not shown. The bill covers online and automatic voter registration through driver license offices (the form asks if the applicant is a citizen and warns that non-citizens commit a felony by applying), a ban on voter-roll purging, and confidentiality of photocopies of identification for voting. It sets no ID rule for voting in person or by mail. Referred to committee 4/8/2025 and not moved since.
subjects: automatic voter registration with citizenship question

findings.motion: HB 958, Election Law Changes, Second Reading (Roll Call #758); passed 66 to 47
findings.note: She voted no on second reading of HB 958. The seventh edition of the bill (https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/PDF/H958v7.pdf) requires driver license offices to proceed with a voter registration only if the applicant states they are a citizen (Section 2.4), requires the State Board of Elections to create a process to remove voters flagged as possible non-citizens by a federal database (Section 2.3), and requires a statement under penalty of perjury on citizenship for registration applications.

findings.motion: HB 958, Election Law Changes, M11 Concur (House vote to concur in the Senate committee substitute, Roll Call #801); passed 62 to 47
findings.note: She voted no on the House vote to concur in the Senate version of HB 958. The bill page shows the concurrence vote and that the bill was then placed on the calendar for 9/2/2026. Same citizenship-on-registration and non-citizen voter-roll provisions as in the seventh edition of the bill.

findings.motion: House concur in Senate committee substitute, H 958 Election Law Changes (62-47)
findings.note: She is listed among the Noes on the final House vote on H 958. The ratified bill (https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/PDF/H958v9.pdf) requires a registration application to state that the applicant is a U.S. citizen before it is processed, with a 30-day sworn-statement fix if the answer is blank, and sets up a process to remove voters flagged as possible non-citizens by a federal database. It was vetoed by the Governor on 2026-08-17 per the bill page.
